html:
Reconstruction was the period after the Civil War, from 1865 to 1877, when the United States tried to rebuild the South and define the rights of four million freed people.

Congress passed the Fourteenth Amendment of 1868, granting citizenship and equal protection of the laws, and the Fifteenth of 1870, barring racial bars to voting. Black men voted and held office; over 600 served in state legislatures and 16 in Congress. The Freedmen's Bureau founded schools.

White Southerners fought back with terror by the Ku Klux Klan and others. In the Compromise of 1877 federal troops left the South, and white rule returned under the Jim Crow laws. The amendments later became the basis of the civil rights era, as in Brown v. Board.
sum: Reconstruction was the period after the Civil War, from 1865 to 1877, when the United States tried to rebuild the South and define the rights of four million freed people.
